findings.source_passage: I tried to will myself to hate this creature, this dragon-man who had kidnapped me and made me his slave, but I couldn't.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'W-what are you doing to me?'
findings.why_it_matters: This internal struggle—the explicit naming of 'dragon-man,' 'kidnapped,' 'slave'—is the interpretive keystone of the seduction scene, establishing the narrator's complicity and moral conflict. The draft alludes to it only in a parenthetical aside ('my traitor body... kidnapped and possession and no'), stripping the full emotional articulation that gives the consent scene its tension.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the direct internal monologue verbalizing 'kidnapped me and made me his slave' so the reader feels the full weight of capitulation rather than a glancing reference.

findings.source_passage: I felt like a caterpillar preparing for a long, comforting nap before emerging as a beautiful butterfly.
findings.source_locator: paragraph ending 'He wrapped his wings around me in a warm embrace'
findings.why_it_matters: The caterpillar/butterfly simile is the chapter's most distinctive figurative image and its only sustained metaphor; it encodes the transformation theme central to the whole book. Its complete absence removes a recognizable, genre-defining moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Reintroduce the caterpillar-to-butterfly simile in the wing-embrace passage; it is short enough to include verbatim within the compression budget.

findings.source_passage: They consumed me like a man starved of food who had finally found his feast.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'He drew the flimsy gown over my head'
findings.why_it_matters: This simile is the chapter's primary voice-establishing rhetorical flourish during the intimate scene and contributes significantly to the erotic register; its loss flattens the narrator's characteristic hyperbolic voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore or closely paraphrase the 'starved man / feast' simile when describing his gaze after removing her dress.

findings.source_passage: "I consider myself only half dragon. My mother was a Maiden like yourself, and my father took her as his bride," he revealed.
findings.source_locator: Early dialogue, after the narrator touches the wings
findings.why_it_matters: The lord's disclosure that he is half-dragon and that his own mother was a Maiden is load-bearing world-building and mirrors the narrator's situation; it is the chapter's central piece of lore and its omission removes a thematically critical parallel.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore this dialogue exchange, including 'My mother was a Maiden like yourself,' before the seduction begins.

findings.source_passage: "So… tight," he gasped. I leaned forward and nibbled at his ear. "So wonderful."
findings.why_it_matters: This brief reciprocal dialogue is the only moment of mutual verbal exchange during the sex scene and gives the narrator an active, not merely receptive, role; its loss slightly reduces her voice in the scene's most intense passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Reintegrate the brief 'So tight / So wonderful' exchange to preserve narrative reciprocity.

summary: Four findings of medium severity (the absent half-dragon lore disclosure, the caterpillar/butterfly simile, the 'starved man/feast' simile, and the full slave-self-reproach) together trigger regeneration; the draft compresses the scene's interpretive and voice-defining material too aggressively.
